Paragraph:
Translation: O son of Prtha, there is no work prescribed for Me within all the three planetary systems. Nor am I in want of anything, nor have I need to obtain anything—and yet I am engaged in work.

Purport (Excerpt): ...Since everything is in full opulence in the Personality of Godhead... there is no duty for the Supreme Personality of Godhead to perform... And yet Lord Krsna is engaged on the Battlefield of Kuruksetra as the leader of the ksatriyas... Although He is above all the regulations... He does not do anything that violates the revealed scriptures.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Explaining why the Supreme, who possesses everything and has no obligations, chooses to engage in active duty.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna shares His own life as an example: though He lacks nothing and has no compulsory duties in the three worlds, He voluntarily stays active in duty to maintain cosmic order and model responsible behavior.
Outcome/Resolution: Arjuna sees that even the Supreme Lord acts continuously for the benefit of others without personal need.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Altruistic Engagement: Working entirely for the benefit of others rather than personal gain
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Voluntary Duty: Embracing responsibilities out of care and purpose rather than obligation
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Unselfish Action: Participating in life fully without needing external rewards

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Na me parthasti kartavyam (No compulsory work exists for the Supreme Lord)
Varta eva ca karmani (Yet continually engaging in active work)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Although Krishna is complete in Himself with no needs or compulsory duties across all worlds, He actively performs work. He sets a direct example showing that spiritual perfection does not mean passive withdrawal from duty.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Engaging in purposeful activity when you don't 'have to' builds resilience and self-worth. Voluntary contribution—working out of care and core values rather than compulsion—fosters deep intrinsic motivation and emotional satisfaction.
